final_candidates.decision_summary: Disrupts the BRCT hydrophobic phosphopeptide-binding groove to ablate DNA repair interactions while preserving the overall BRCT tandem fold.
Abolishes BARD1 heterodimerization and E3 ubiquitin ligase activity essential for tumor suppression while maintaining the core RING domain architecture.
Directly eliminates critical phosphate coordination in the BRCT phosphopeptide cleft, knocking out DNA-repair signaling without destabilizing protein folding.

stop_reason.detail: Target phenotype is fully addressed by validated canonical separation-of-function and loss-of-function candidates.

history.rationale: R1699 forms essential direct electrostatic contacts with the target pSer residue in BRCT phosphopeptide recognition; mutating to Gln selectively abrogates DNA repair while preserving BRCT structural integrity.
R1699Q is a canonical functional-knockout mutation that selectively ablates phosphopeptide binding without destabilizing the BRCT fold.
Bulky tryptophan substitution at R1699 disrupts the phosphopeptide-binding pocket of the BRCT domain, severely impairing homology-directed repair and tumor suppressor activity.
R1699W effectively impairs BRCT pocket function with high pathogenicity (0.824), though slightly more sterically disruptive than R1699Q.
Canonical pathogenic BRCT variant that abolishes phosphopeptide binding and homology-directed DNA repair, acting as a definitive loss-of-function driver.
M1775R shows strong predicted LOF pathogenicity (0.893) and is clinically validated to abolish BRCT phosphopeptide recognition while maintaining structural integrity.
Clinically validated pathogenic RING finger mutation that abrogates BARD1-dependent ubiquitin ligase function and homology-directed repair.
C61G demonstrates exceptionally high LOF pathogenicity (0.990) by disrupting BARD1 interaction and E3 ubiquitin ligase function.
Zn-coordinating cysteine mutation in the RING domain that abolishes BRCA1 tumor suppressor activity and DNA repair while maintaining local expression.
C64Y disrupts zinc coordination in the RING domain with extremely high predicted pathogenicity (0.993).
W1837 defines the hydrophobic +3 Phe-binding pocket in the BRCT repeat; substitution to Arg abolishes phosphopeptide engagement and DNA damage response.
W1837R shows near-maximal LOF pathogenicity (0.998) in AlphaMissense, confirming complete loss of tumor suppressor activity.
Well-documented pathogenic BRCT mutation introducing an unfavorable charge into the hydrophobic interface, causing loss of DNA repair capability.
A1708E shows high pathogenicity (0.971) indicating robust loss of BRCT-mediated DNA repair activity.
S1655 hydrogen bonds directly with the phosphate moiety of bound partner peptides; Ala substitution diminishes BRCT phosphopeptide recognition.
Rejected because AlphaMissense classifies S1655A as benign (0.337), failing to reliably abolish BRCA1 tumor-suppressor activity.

rejection.reason: Rejected because AlphaMissense classifies S1655A as benign (0.337), failing to reliably abolish BRCA1 tumor-suppressor activity.

history.rationale: Pathogenic variant placing a bulky aromatic residue in the phosphate-binding pocket, sterically occluding phosphorylated partner interactions.
Supported by high pathogenicity (0.894) due to bulky aromatic substitution in the BRCT N-terminal region.
Disrupts key polar interactions with the phosphopeptide phosphate group, impairing downstream recruitment in homology-directed repair.
Confirmed pathogenic (0.910), retained as a solid candidate in the BRCT phosphopeptide cleft.
